title: Radial Econ Accelerator: coordinated batching/caching/quantization initiative
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Initiative charter to align product, eng, and DX for a coordinated program of batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization profiles aimed at sustained unit-cost reduction for latency-sensitive hosted workloads. The goal is a reproducible experiment grid, a rollout playbook that preserves tail-latency SLOs, and integrated console signals for automated rollouts and fallback. This ticket tracks roadmap milestones, cross-team dependencies, OKRs, and experiment outcomes for the next three cycles.
success_metrics:
- 20% median token cost reduction for low-SLA hosted routes
- <5% regression rate in quality for control prompt suites (measured by eval signals)
- Maintain p95 latency within 1.2x of baseline
- 3 validated model/quant profiles with production guardrails
milestones: M1: Experiment grid defined and prioritized (batch sizes, caching TTLs, quant profiles) - target 2026-01-15
M2: Infra enablement completed (batching knobs + kv cache hooks + quant profiles) - target 2026-01-31
M3: Field experiments (canary cohorts) running with observability dashboards - target 2026-02-14
M4: Rollout playbook + automation for rollback/fallback integrated into Console - target 2026-02-28
M5: Post-rollout retrospective and OKR measurement - target 2026-03-07
rollout_plan: Start with non-critical hosted routes (low-traffic assistant templates) in canary buckets. Use progressive exposure (1%, 5%, 25%) with automated quality gates tied to eval sets and per-route latency SLO checks. If quality or latency regressions exceed thresholds, trigger automatic fallback to baseline model/quant profile and open incident for triage. After canary success, expand to dedicated and enterprise tenant cohorts with opt-in migration windows.
risks: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization profiles causing increased hallucination rates
Unexpected p99 latency spikes when batching thresholds interact with real-time traffic patterns
Telemetry gaps that delay detection of subtle degradations across multi-tenant workloads
Rollout automation misconfiguration leading to overexposure
